title: Friggione
subtitle: Slow-cooked Bolognese pepper and onion stew
excerpt: A Bolognese condiment of peppers and onions cooked very slowly in tomatoes until everything softens into a sweet, jammy stew. Good with grilled meat, eggs, or bruschetta.
sourceNotes: Friggione is a traditional condiment from Bologna in Emilia-Romagna. The long slow cook is essential to the dish.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freezes well for up to 3 months in small jars or containers. Defrost overnight and reheat gently.
recipe.batchNotes: Easy to double or triple. Make a large batch and serve across the week with different things.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Improves significantly after a day in the fridge. Make ahead and reheat over a low heat.

content.text: Friggione is a slow-cooked pepper and onion stew from Bologna. The onion must cook for a long time before anything else goes in. Patience here is what separates a good friggione from a sharp, undercooked one.

items.prepNote: about 2 large, deseeded and sliced into strips

content.text: Heat the oil in a wide pan over a low heat. Add the sliced onion and salt. Stir to coat. Cover with a lid and cook for 20 minutes, stirring every 5 minutes.
Remove the lid. Continue cooking for 10 more minutes until the onion is soft, pale, and sweet. It should not brown.
Add the pepper strips. Stir well. Cook on a low heat for 10 minutes until the peppers soften.
Add the tinned tomatoes, sugar, and black pepper. Crush the tomatoes with the spoon.
Simmer uncovered on a low heat for 20 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the sauce is thick and jammy. There should be very little liquid left.
Taste and adjust the salt and sugar. Scatter with torn basil if using. Serve warm or at room temperature.

items.symptom: The onions have browned and taste sharp.
items.cause: The heat was too high during the first stage.
items.fix: Friggione needs a very low heat. The onions should collapse and sweeten, not colour. Reduce the heat and add a splash of water.

items.cause: It was not cooked for long enough after the tomatoes were added.
items.fix: Continue simmering uncovered on a low heat until the excess liquid evaporates and the stew is thick and jammy.

items.symptom: The peppers are still firm in the finished dish.
items.cause: They were added too late or the heat was too low.
items.fix: Cook the peppers for a full 10 minutes before adding the tomatoes. Raise the heat slightly if they are not softening.
